QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_5

question.text: What is 'contango' and 'backwardation' in futures markets?

answer.text: Contango: futures price above spot price (normal carry-cost market). Backwardation: futures price below spot price (demand for immediate delivery exceeds forward supply)
Contango: futures price below spot price. Backwardation: futures price above spot price
Contango refers to rising prices. Backwardation refers to falling prices
These terms only apply to commodity markets, not financial derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: Contango (futures above spot) is the normal state when carrying costs are positive. Backwardation (futures below spot) occurs when there is high demand for immediate delivery or a high convenience yield. At expiry, futures and spot prices converge regardless of whether the market was in contango or backwardation. The Trap: Contango/backwardation describe the spot-versus-futures relationship, not the direction of price changes. These terms apply to ALL futures markets — equity, currency, interest-rate, and commodity — not just commodities. Note: Replaced ambiguous "<" / ">" expressions with "above"/"below" wording in both the keyed option and the second option so the comparison is no longer truncated; distributor/cross-exam framing removed.
